operator_io_quirks: Table name 'voice-actors' contains a hyphen and must be double-quoted everywhere; column 'voice-actor' likewise.
Column names contain spaces, brackets, digits: 'Studio Entertainment[NI 1]', 'Disney Interactive[NI 3][Rev 1]', 'Walt Disney Parks and Resorts'.
Mixed-case identifiers: 'Year', 'Total', 'MPAA_rating', 'movie_title' vs 'Year' — case-insensitive lookup required.

FK cycle: characters.hero -> voice-actors.character, voice-actors.movie -> characters.movie_title, director.name -> characters.movie_title. Table-level cycle characters<->voice-actors must be broken deterministically.
director.name is PK and FK to characters.movie_title (1:1-ish); child PK values must come from parent, not fresh.
movies_total_gross has composite PK (movie_title, release_date) and FK movie_title -> characters.movie_title; PK member is also FK.
release_date stored as TEXT in two different formats: characters '21-Dec-37' (dd-Mon-yy) vs movies_total_gross 'Jan 25, 1961' (Mon dd, yyyy). Declared TEXT so TS dispatches String, not Date.
total_gross / inflation_adjusted_gross are TEXT holding '$184,925,485' — currency strings, not numbers.
Disney Media Networks is TEXT but holds numeric-looking strings '359','4,142','6522' (mixed comma formatting).
revenue.Year INTEGER PK with values 1991..2016; Number fuzzer will generate ints in [-10^0,10^0] range unless scale parsed — declared 'INTEGER' has no (a,b) args so scale=0.
High null rates: Disney Interactive[NI 3][Rev 1] 0.538, villian 0.179, song 0.161, Disney Media Networks 0.115 — but notnull=0 everywhere so TS won't enforce.
voice-actors.voice-actor has literal string 'None' as a value (not SQL NULL) — distinct from NULL storage.
operator_ts_expectations: All TEXT columns -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20, plus 5 sampled originals, plus contaminate suffix/prefix/drop. Movie titles, dates, dollar amounts all become gibberish strings.
release_date (TEXT) -> String fuzzer, so '21-Dec-37' and 'Jan 25, 1961' formats are NOT preserved; date-comparison queries will mostly fail to match.
total_gross '$184,925,485' -> String fuzzer; numeric/currency comparisons in gold SQL will not match generated values -> likely FN.
revenue.Year INTEGER -> Number(scale=0): range [-1,1] ints, perturbed +-1/+-2; original 1991..2016 never reproduced -> year-range queries FN.
revenue REAL columns -> Number(scale=0) too (no args): range [-1,1] floats; original values 700..6000 -> FN on magnitude filters.
Disney Media Networks TEXT -> String; numeric-looking originals lost.

FK characters.hero -> voice-actors.character: TS draws from parent's FINAL character values (922 distinct names like 'Abu'); plausible but hero names in original are character names too, so ties may survive.
director.name PK+FK: TS fills from characters.movie_title then drops PK dups; director.director is String -> random names, original 29 distinct directors lost -> director-name queries FN.

movies_total_gross composite PK (movie_title, release_date): TS drops duplicate PK tuples; since both are String-fuzzed, collisions rare, but FK movie_title drawn from characters.movie_title gives plausible titles.
String fuzzer contaminate (0.5 prob) adds/drops chars -> near-miss values that break equality joins -> FP on join-heavy queries.
Empty-string values in genre/MPAA_rating originals: String fuzzer may produce '' via length-0 draw, so empty-string predicates may accidentally match.
voice-actors.voice-actor 'None' string: String fuzzer treats as normal element; queries filtering IS NULL vs ='None' diverge.
